summary: Add a provider-neutral, redacted financial evidence and completeness boundary around existing order, payment, settlement, inventory, FX and advertising sources without creating a second ledger.

impacts.evidence: Bank accounts, statements, source records, findings and backfill jobs are scoped by organization/workspace and forced RLS; repository queries establish scope inside a transaction.
Only masked account references, opaque SecretProvider references, amounts, dates, status and digests are accepted; credentials, raw statements and PII are excluded.
Completeness summary, source evidence, bank account, statement preview/commit and findings are additive OpenAPI operations with regenerated SDKs.
No new public event is introduced; canonical financial ledgers, outbox and existing calculation snapshots remain authoritative.
Provider-neutral source kinds and a read-only MCP completeness tool expose quality without provider-specific branches or credential access.
Migration 54 is expand-only, backup-gated through the migration catalog, tenant-scoped and adds immutable evidence/manifests plus bounded backfill job metadata.
Full account numbers and secret-like values are rejected at core/SQL boundaries; writes require permission, idempotency and sensitive audit; no API returns SecretProvider references.
Source imports are sensitive audited actions and adjustments remain outside this read/evidence boundary; MCP cannot import, adjust or declare completeness.
Source digest, provider reference, period, statement relation and audit correlation are retained while append-only source evidence cannot be mutated.
Stable source identity deduplication, conflict detection, findings queue and idempotent statement/account/source commits preserve both sides of a mismatch.
No caller-controlled egress or webhook endpoint is added; live bank and marketplace adapters remain separate qualified connector work.
Summary exposes coverage, source freshness and open findings; bounded list endpoints and a dedicated static qualification gate support operations.
Source evidence and statements are append-only; source failure leaves previous snapshots intact, and release docs require disabling imports/recalculation rather than destructive rollback.
Core/API/MCP tests, OpenAPI runtime parity, migration/catalog checks, SDK generation, frontend contract and synthetic financial gate cover the repository boundary.
